historyCoverage: Selected source-verified provincial vote-intention releases from 2017 to 2026, not an exhaustive poll database. Gaps are not filled with inferred observations.
basis: Decided and leaning voters; one latest release per pollster in the 14 days ending at the snapshot date. No sample weighting. An average appears only for parties reported by at least two pollsters. Min/max are observed poll values, not confidence intervals.

releases.note: The pollster reports 20% initially undecided among all respondents. The shares shown here use decided and leaning voters. Independent/non-affiliated is separately reported.
The publisher also reports 3% for parties it does not separate. Those votes are not assigned to any party in this dataset.
Earlier Angus Reid release; kept for history, excluded from current mean because the September 24 release is newer.
Outside the 14-day summary window. Different decided-voter wording; shown as historical context only.
Outside the 14-day summary window. Publisher groups 3.6% as another party; it is not assigned to a registered party here.

releases.question: QP5/QP6: provincial election tomorrow, decided and leaning voters
releases.note: Primary table QP5/QP6 continues from page 7 to page 8. Total unweighted sample is 755; weighted total is 761. The 6% other-party response is grouped and is not assigned to named parties. Historical context, outside the current mean.

releases.question: Provincial election held today: decided voters, actual-party ballot
releases.note: Uses the ordinary ballot question on page 3, not the separate hypothetical ballot including a revived BC Liberal party. Another party / independent is grouped at 2%. The page publication date is June 8; its body dateline says June 6. Historical context, outside the current mean.

releases.question: Q_Land2: election tomorrow, decided voters
releases.note: Q_Land2 reports decided voters, not the decided-and-leaning wording used in some other ARI releases. The decided base is 595 unweighted / 600 weighted. Other party is grouped at 4%; rounding leaves the full reported distribution at 99%. Uses the May 5 release dateline and document date; the webpage header is May 4.

releases.question: QP5/QP6: provincial election tomorrow, decided and leaning voters
releases.note: Uses the April 1 release dateline and PDF date; the webpage header says March 31. Tables show 500 unweighted / 499 weighted respondents, while the release calls the sample 499. The named-party figures are 44/42/9; the same table reports other party at 7%, producing an inconsistent total of 102%. That grouped residual is not allocated or silently corrected. Requires review before promotion.
Ordinary provincial voting intention from the original release. Unspecified residual responses are not allocated to named parties.

Fieldwork preceded OneBC's formation. A proposed unnamed party featuring Brodie, Kealy and Armstrong received 1%; it is not relabelled as OneBC here. Ballot options therefore differ from later releases.
Other parties and independent candidates are grouped at 3%; no named-party values are inferred from that group.

Other parties and independents are grouped at 1%; rounding is preserved.
